clips.send: Four rams. The rams’ bodies form the belly; their heads stick out. A ram stands at each of the four corners; its curled horns and head project from the shoulder. Late Shang dynasty; unearthed at Ningxiang, Hunan; 58.3 cm tall. Its unusual shape and exquisite craft make it a masterpiece of Shang bronze casting.

clips.send: Inscription “后母戊”. Three characters cast inside the wall. The inner wall carries three characters: 后母戊 (Hou Mu Wu). A Shang king had it cast to offer sacrifices to his mother, named “Wu”. Characters cast on bronzes are called bronze script (jinwen).

clips.send: The evolution of Chinese script: oracle-bone script, bronze script (cast on bronzes), small seal script (unified by the Qin), clerical script (Han), regular script.

clips.send: About 2070 BCE Yu founded the Xia, China’s first dynasty. After Yu died his son Qi took the throne: hereditary rule replaced abdication — “shared by all” became “owned by one family”.

clips.send: Late Western Zhou rule decayed: in 841 BCE the people of the capital rose up. In 771 BCE the Western Zhou fell. The next year (770 BCE) King Ping moved the capital east to Luoyi — the Eastern Zhou began.

clips.send: Ding body and taotie pattern. A rectangular ritual cauldron of the late Shang. Cast in the late Shang dynasty; unearthed in 1939 at Anyang, Henan. It weighs 832.84 kg and stands 133 cm tall: the heaviest ancient Chinese bronze yet found. The walls are covered with beast-face (taotie) patterns on a background of thunder-cloud spirals.

clips.send: Four column legs. Hold up 832 kg — and leave room for a fire. Four thick hollow column legs support the vessel. A ding was first a cooking pot; later bronze ding became ritual vessels and symbols of power. Each leg is decorated with a beast face near the top.

clips.send: To secure its rule, the Zhou king gave land and people to royal relatives, meritorious officials and nobles of earlier dynasties, who set up vassal states such as Lu, Qi, Yan, Jin and Song. The lords had to obey, pay tribute, fight for the king and protect the royal house.

clips.send: 为了巩固统治，西周实行分封制：周王把土地和人民分封给王族、功臣和先代的贵族，让他们建立诸侯国，如鲁、齐、燕、晋、宋等。诸侯要服从周王命令，定期朝贡，带兵随从周王作战，保卫王室。

clips.send: 看地图（示意图）：河南偃师二里头遗址可能是夏朝的都城。约前 1600 年，商汤灭夏，建立商朝。约前 1300 年，盘庚迁都到殷（今河南安阳），此后商朝统治稳定下来，商朝也称“殷”“殷商”。

clips.send: 易错点：世袭制始于夏朝（禹的儿子启继位），分封制是西周实行的；不要把“世袭制代替禅让制”说成是商朝或西周的事。

clips.send: 后母戊鼎：四根柱足。 撑起 832 千克，下面还能生火。 四根粗壮的柱足支撑起整个鼎。 鼎最初是煮肉的炊具，后来青铜鼎成为祭祀用的礼器和权力的象征。 柱足上部装饰着兽面纹。

clips.send: 约公元前 2070 年，禹建立夏朝，这是我国历史上第一个王朝。禹死后，他的儿子启继承王位，世袭制代替了禅让制，“公天下”变成了“家天下”。
